items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-01
items.q: Old man Lloyd Fritz was a bass. And, Junior was a triumphant... There were two men who used to come over and play with their band.

ctx.x: What about this guy, who's called Fritz?

Fritz had a good term, but not compared to none of the people. He was a... Fritz had a term, something like... I used to say something like Edmund Hall or something. Sure. That's sort of a tone yet. But, uh, it was very fast. And you knew what he was doing. But for a tone, you can have a tone like it. You take Edmund Hall or a tone like it, but it was more... Raw than some new musicians that you would get. Although I'm not knocking them easy at first class musicians. Stone was not the same with me.
Yeah. What about Fritz's ideas? Well, I think... Man, I think it was Chris...

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-01
items.q: Because Fris and they had their own band. And Fris, they wouldn't even because they'd ever want to have a band with me, so they'd make more money than paying, you know.

ctx.x: When would he finally start doing that? Was that towards the end of his life?

You know, that wasn't towards the end of his life. He did it so often. He told it to you. He was just put on the shelf. Because I came over here. I was there in Manorville. Let me talk. And I came over here after the band is all where Edmund Hall left the band. And I got it in Black in town. So, did you see the picture? With George Washington. I don't know. What it matter? Just on Facebook. I don't know. I'm going to finish that. And it was. We call it Facel. That's why Zoothing all of them got it in the way they…
How long were you doing that? Some of you haven't had everybody to do it for your counseling?
